baselineBehavior.requested: world/alias-to-world (a junction whose target is the world)

D1.expectedBehavior: REFUSED — lexical identity with the world is required, so a mutable indirection is never approved from its current target
D1.securityImpact: an admitted alias is a path whose meaning the model can change after the decision; the child's pre-step instruction discovery would then traverse a tree the guard never examined

contrast.note: the current guard refuses THIS alias because its canonical target is outside the world; the defect is that the decision is made from the target at all

D2.expectedBehavior: a digest of the UTF-8 bytes of the persisted assistant text actually extracted and scored
D2.measurementImpact: the receipt identifies no answer. Two different answers, and an absent answer, all hash to the same value, so the artifact cannot distinguish a real extraction from a missing one

D3.expectedBehavior: a mandatory ACE whose policy mask could not be decoded is UNVERIFIED: parsing reports unreadable, ensureRoot refuses to write, and no policy bit is ever computed from an assumed zero mask
D3.securityImpact: the parser reported a trusted label, and the planned write replaced an unknown policy with NO_READ_UP alone — every pre-existing policy bit on the object would be discarded

D4.note: This is a static property of the generator, NOT a live exploit. §7.7 requires the dynamic falsifiers to exercise the NEW admission code, which is where they run.

baselineBehavior.duplicateIdInRealReport: HR-25 appears twice in the R1-HR report with different statements; both rows are preserved, and no reconciliation is recorded

D4.expectedBehavior: each authoritative artifact is bound to a run identity (executed code HEAD, tree, command, exit code, runtime, DSH identity, selection, artifact digest) and the gate rejects missing, stale, tampered or LIMIT-relabelled input
D4.measurementImpact: a report produced against different code, or by a different DSH, or a disclosed LIMIT, can be recorded as a successful assertion about the code being qualified
